The question of whether curved TV screens are better for viewing is genuinely contested across the retrieved evidence. On one hand, some sources and studies argue in favor of curved TVs: [d1] found that visual presence was 18% higher for 2D content and 9% higher for 3D content on a curved TV compared to a flat screen at 2 m viewing distance, though results varied with conditions. [d2] claims curved TVs "create an engaging viewing experience that is difficult to replicate with flat-screen sets," citing wider field of view, reduced glare, and no sweet spot issue. [d3] similarly states that "studies have documented that the design of curved monitors may actually reduce strain on your eyes," and highlights crisper images and greater immersion. [d5] adds that curved TVs reduce geometric distortion "by approximately 50% at a typical 8-foot viewing distance" compared to flat TVs. On the other hand, [d4] explicitly concludes that "curved TVs are not that much better than flat-screen TVs" and that "most reviewers don't believe the premium price tag of a curved TV is worth it," noting a narrower sweet spot and new viewing problems. [d8] argues that curved TVs are "only ideal for ONE viewer at a time right in the center," cause distortion of flat lines, and do not benefit picture quality for most viewers. [d6] similarly notes that the broader field of view benefit "can only be experienced when you're positioned in the right spot, the front and center." Overall, the evidence reflects genuinely conflicting opinions and research outcomes, with no clear universal verdict on whether curved TVs are better for viewing.
